$$\frac{d}{dt}\phi_t^X(p) = X\bigl(\phi_t^X(p)\bigr), \qquad \phi_0^X = \mathrm{id}_M.$$

$$d\rho(X)(f) = \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} \rho\bigl(\phi_t^X\bigr)(f).$$

Since $(\phi_t^X)^{-1} = \phi_{-t}^X$, we have
$$\rho\bigl(\phi_t^X\bigr)(f) = f \circ \phi_{-t}^X.$$

Therefore, for each $p \in M$:
$$d\rho(X)(f)(p) = \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} f\bigl(\phi_{-t}^X(p)\bigr).$$

Setting $g(t) = f(\phi_{-t}^X(p))$ and differentiating via the chain rule:
$$g'(t) = df_{\phi_{-t}^X(p)} \cdot \frac{d}{dt}\phi_{-t}^X(p) = df_{\phi_{-t}^X(p)} \cdot \bigl(-X(\phi_{-t}^X(p))\bigr).$$

Evaluating at $t = 0$ (where $\phi_0^X(p) = p$):
$$g'(0) = df_p \cdot (-X(p)) = -X(f)(p),$$

where $X(f) = df \cdot X$ is the directional derivative (Lie derivative) of $f$ along $X$. Thus:

$$\boxed{d\rho(X)(f) = -X(f).}$$

Now checking the homomorphism property $d\rho([X,Y]_{\mathfrak{g}}) = [d\rho(X), d\rho(Y)]$:

**Left side:**
$$d\rho([X,Y]_{\mathfrak{g}})(f) = -[X,Y]_{\mathfrak{g}}(f) = -(-[X,Y]_{\mathrm{std}})(f) = [X,Y]_{\mathrm{std}}(f) = X(Yf) - Y(Xf).$$

**Right side** (commutator of endomorphisms):
$$[d\rho(X), d\rho(Y)](f) = d\rho(X)\bigl(d\rho(Y)(f)\bigr) - d\rho(Y)\bigl(d\rho(X)(f)\bigr)$$
$$= d\rho(X)(-Yf) - d\rho(Y)(-Xf) = -X(-Yf) - (-Y(-Xf)) = X(Yf) - Y(Xf).$$

Both sides agree: $[d\rho(X), d\rho(Y)](f) = X(Yf) - Y(Xf) = d\rho([X,Y]_{\mathfrak{g}})(f)$. $\checkmark$

$$X \cdot f \;=\; d\rho(X)(f) \;=\; -X(f),$$
i.e., the **negative of the directional derivative** (Lie derivative) of $f$ along $X$. The minus sign is the infinitesimal manifestation of the inverse $F^{-1}$ appearing in the representation $\rho(F)(f) = f \circ F^{-1}$.

$$d\rho(X)(f) = \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} \rho\bigl(\phi_t^X\bigr)(f).$$

Since $(\phi_t^X)^{-1} = \phi_{-t}^X$, we have
$$\rho\bigl(\phi_t^X\bigr)(f) = f \circ \phi_{-t}^X.$$

$$d\rho(X)(f)(p) = \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} f\bigl(\phi_{-t}^X(p)\bigr).$$
